study.question: Can a single dense context matrix trained from exactly the inherited rank96 factor product preserve the strongest current click AUC while reducing trainable storage and measured prediction cost? Does the effect of replacing continued factorized optimization depend on rank96 versus rank88 initialization?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: native96 AUC0.6675003890552496 exceeds native88 0.6671251297972951. Output-heavy factor gauges, rank88 energy restoration and DCT coordinates did not recover the gap; DCT rank-by-basis interaction is -0.000046423337253465. The older separate dense control used the full112 initial matrix and reached0.6672902815744913, so it did not hold effective initialization fixed. Hypothesis: spectral truncation at initialization may provide enough of the factorized model's useful bias that continued two-factor training is unnecessary. Materializing the identical fresh rank96 product into one freely trainable dense map might retain quality while removing factor overparameterization. This is unverified and may fail because factor geometry/continued rank restriction, auxiliary context gradients or BF16 behavior matter. Reproduced identical-seed native results are reliability evidence, not repeated independent mechanism support.

This local study removes continued factors at fixed initial product in only the buy context block; no HiFormer attention/task-token architecture or reproduction claim.

Build the exact inherited fresh balanced rank-r factors and materialize W_r=B_r@A_r in FP32 with autocast disabled. All nonconstructor methods remain AST-identical to the parent. Dense96 and dense88 are unrestricted dense maps after updates, not low-rank architectures. predictions: Selection criterion is frozen prospectively: dense96_product must reach AUC>=max(same-round factor96 AUC-0.0001,0.6674003890552496). Absolute floor uses current incumbent0.6675003890552496; this is stricter than merely retaining original joint entry0.666753547526167. No unavailable historical preservation criterion is assumed.

Analytic context matrix count: rank96 factors96*(192+112)=29184; rank88 factors26752; dense21504. Predicted dense96 total31986099/dense192883/embedding31793216 versus factor96 total31993779/dense200563; saving7680 (3.83% of dense,0.0240% of all Parameters). Dense88 has the same dense count, saving5248 versus factor88. Host measurements are authoritative.

One dense context GEMM replaces two factor GEMMs in training and prediction. Analytic block multiply-add count falls29184->21504 at rank96 (26.32%) and26752->21504 at rank88 (19.62%); this does not imply end-to-end speedup. Require measured model-only p50 <=0.98 times contemporaneous factor96 and p95 <=1.01 times control for a screening utility pass; report total inference seconds/throughput and training/allocated GPU/wall cost separately.

For rank-dependent mechanism evidence predeclare interaction I=(dense88-factor88)-(dense96-factor96). I>=0.0002 is a consequential recovery signal only; report all four cells and both rank contrasts, including opposite signs and null outcomes. Dense88 remains control-only.

Report click and all three auxiliary AUC/logloss plus auxiliary mean, counts and inherited history slices. Existing click-focused models have substantial auxiliary degradation relative to DIN; a click preservation claim is not a claim of preserving all tasks. Three paired seeds and paired user-cluster uncertainty, if supported by authorized host feedback, are needed before stronger conclusions; no independent-row intervals.
falsifiers: Dense96 click AUC violates either frozen preservation bound; keeping the initial product did not suffice in this implementation.

Measured parameter count fails to drop by7680, factor/SVD/full-template storage survives, optimizer misses context_weight, or any information/mask/gradient boundary changes: reject implementation before interpretation.
Dense96 p50/p95 fails the frozen cost condition, or repeated matched measurements reverse it: no demonstrated prediction-cost utility even with fewer parameters.

If the current factor controls fail to reproduce accepted AUC under the frozen protocol, resolve the discrepancy before comparing scientific effects; missing prerequisites and host failure are not mechanism counterevidence.

An apparent dense88 advantage with small/opposite interaction or inconsistent paired seeds does not support rank-specific optimization recovery. Both dense cells failing closes this bounded replacement, without a universal necessity claim.
alternative_explanations: Dense and factored updates are intentionally different: parameter count, rank constraint, AdamW coordinate geometry/weight decay and global dense clipping all change together. This is an aggregate parameterization replacement, not isolation of one optimizer mechanism.
One versus two BF16 GEMMs can produce different finite-precision activations despite matching FP32 weight product; no exact BF16 output equivalence is assumed.
Runtime noise, shared host load and a single training seed limit attribution. Identical-seed reruns are reproducibility checks, not independent support.

SVD truncation affects the initial effective matrix even though no data informs it. Dense products can immediately regain rank, so success could reflect added functional capacity with fewer redundant coefficients rather than redundant predictive directions.
Auxiliary buy gradients and shared dense clipping can alter click learning; the factorial does not identify those mediators individually. Default summed BCE and optimizer rules stay unchanged.

Model-only batch latency can be dominated by common embedding/history operators; total inference wall includes loading. The native96 wall time ranged24.924 to28.306 seconds across accepted runs with the same AUC, so historical timing alone is inadequate.

Original whole-window filtering/static vocabularies and released delayed-action visibility remain benchmark assumptions; no production point-in-time validity or advertisement-specific conversion attribution is established.
